practices_evaluation.justification: The test performs two 'Act' operations: constructs a Grafo in @Before (setup) and constructs another Grafo in the test, and asserts both. There are multiple operations/assertion targets in a single test, violating single-behavior atomicity.

The class uses @Before to create a fresh Grafo instance for each test (setUp), avoiding shared mutable state across tests. The test uses only local variables and the instance variable initialized in @Before.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: Only a single happy-path test exists in the class; there is no test for error/exceptional scenarios. Per rules, a class with <2 test methods and no exception tests is non-compliant.
The test only verifies construction of Grafo with no numeric or range inputs; there are no obvious boundary values to exercise in this specific test method.
The class extracts setup into an @Before helper (setUp) which prevents duplication and improves modularity. The test method is short and no duplicated setup code is present.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The test method is short (<20 lines), linear, and contains no loops or complex conditionals, meeting the small and focused requirement.
Assertions are superficial (only assertNotNull checks). The test does not verify multiple properties of the created object; it lacks comprehensive assertions to detect deeper faults.
No @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out @Test methods are present. Tests are active and runnable.
Class-level Javadoc includes 'Tests REQ-001', providing traceability to a requirement ID.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: The test uses a timeout (@Test(timeout = 4000)), indicating an explicit timing constraint; per decision rules this qualifies as an explicit performance-related test usage.
The test method name 'test0' is generic and does not follow descriptive naming conventions (methodName_scenario_expectedResult). Although there is Javadoc, the method name itself is not descriptive.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: The presence of EvoSuite artifacts (EvoRunner, EvoRunnerParameters, EvoAssertions), and the generic test name 'test0' indicate generated or heavily automated test origins and verbose test generation patterns.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The test suite contains a minimal happy-path test only; there is no evidence of Given-When-Then structure beyond comments or of prioritized scenario coverage (no edge/error cases).

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test interacts only with the public constructor and does not access private fields or use reflection; it verifies public behavior rather than implementation internals.
Assertions include descriptive failure messages in assertNotNull calls and use specific assertion methods rather than generic assertTrue, meeting the requirement for clear assertions.
Comments are minimal, explain intent (e.g., setup intent, given/when/then), and there is no commented-out code. Class Javadoc provides meaningful context.
The test contains no sources of non-determinism (no Random, no current time usage, no Thread.sleep). The @Before setup ensures consistent state per test.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test uses @Before to create a fresh Grafo per test and does not persist external resources or modify static state; no cleanup is necessary for the shown operations.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: There are no @Tag/@Category annotations. Given the class contains only a single, very small test, marking categorization as not-applicable per decision rules for tiny test classes.
